text:
IncidentBot: paging: high tail latency observed for /v1/generate on prod (p95 > 2.5s). Triggered at 17:03 UTC. Auto-mitigation: routed 30% traffic to fallback-small model.
Maya Patel: seeing it in dashboards, thanks. rolling logs now — will start triage.
Ken O'Connor: grabbing the bridge. joining in 2m. @Priya can you look at routing/variant fallbacks?
Priya Singh: on it. initial check: kube nodes for model-serving pool show normal CPU/GPU utilization. no obvious pod restarts.
Liam Chen: I see increased request queueing on the large-model fleet — autoscaler lagging. suspect spike in long-context requests.
Maya Patel: confirmed long-context tail — lots of 8k+ token requests from batch job we didn't expect (from partner ingest).
SRE Pager: IncidentBot updated: incident severity set to Sev2. Notifying oncall rotation.
Ken O'Connor: mitigation task: set temporary rate limit for partner route to 10r/s. Priya can you apply?
Priya Singh: applying rate limit now. curl snippet to update proxy: ```
POST https://proxy.api/config
{"route":"/partner-gen","rate_limit":10}
```
Priya Singh: applied. traffic dropped and p95 down to ~1.1s within 90s.
Maya Patel: nice. can we also pin partner to small-model variant to reduce token compute?
Liam Chen: small-model gives worse quality, but acceptable for ingest. I'll add routing rule to prefer fallback-small for /partner-gen.
Priya Singh: doing that now. config change: ```
route.rules.partner-gen = { "preferred_model":"fallback-small","max_variant_ttl":600 }
```
Priya Singh: done. metrics look stable.
Ken O'Connor: post-incident next steps: schedule postmortem, action items, update runbook for autoscaler thresholds and partner onboarding checks.
Maya Patel: agreed. Quick postmortem schedule proposal: async timeline doc + 30m sync tomorrow 16:00 UTC. who can own the postmortem?
Liam Chen: I can own the writeup (root cause + timeline). Assign me.
Priya Singh: I'll own remediation item: add route-level admission control + preflight token-length sampling.
Ken O'Connor: I'll own runbook updates and can drive a follow-up on autoscaler tuning.
SRE Pager: action items summary (auto): 1) write postmortem doc (owner: Liam) 2) add runbook section for model-variant fallback policy and partner throttles (owner: Ken) 3) implement admission control preflight and sampling (owner: Priya) 4) autoscaler tuning PR and canary (owner: Ken) 5) communicate partner rate limit and ask for backfill scheduling (owner: Maya).
Maya Patel: for the postmortem doc — use our postmortem template (link: https://redwood.internal/postmortem-template). include timeline, customer impact, mitigation timeline.
Liam Chen: noted. I'll start timeline draft and paste here.
Liam Chen: timeline draft: 
- 17:02 UTC: p95 spikes observed in Datadog for /v1/generate
- 17:03 UTC: IncidentBot page fired; fallback routing engaged automatically (30% to small)
- 17:04-17:05 UTC: triage started; team on bridge
- 17:07 UTC: identified partner traffic spike with many >8k token requests
- 17:10 UTC: rate limit applied to partner route
- 17:12 UTC: route pref set to fallback-small for partner
- 17:14 UTC: p95 returned to ~1.1s; service stabilized
- 17:40 UTC: monitoring verified stability and incident declared mitigated
Maya Patel: solid. add customer impact: briefly increased latency for all customers hitting large-model variants; estimated affected requests ~12k, impacted downstream partners A and B.
Priya Singh: remediation details: implement admission control to reject or sample >6k token requests for non-whitelisted routes; also add a preflight header X-Client-Token-Length that proxies can sample.
Ken O'Connor: runbook edits: update "oncall triage checklist" to include: check model-serving autoscaler status, check recent routing policy changes, verify variant fallback is healthy, and confirm partner admission controls. I'll draft diff.
Maya Patel: also add a small play to coordination with account/sales for partners sending heavy backfill loads — we need an onboarding checklist.
Liam Chen: for regression prevention: add an alert on sudden increase in >4k token requests (rate of change), and low-lag on autoscaler scaling events.
Priya Singh: I'll add a config PR for the admission control. snippet for sampling rule: ```
admission.sample > {
  predicate: request.body.token_count > 6000 && route not in whitelist
  action: sample(rate=0.5)
}
```
Priya Singh: filing PR now: https://git.redwood/svc/proxy/pull/789 (WIP).
Ken O'Connor: scheduling: postmortem doc due EOD tomorrow, runbook PR due in 3 business days, admission-control merged in 5 business days with canary.
Maya Patel: can someone ping product/partner success to coordinate message to partner? I'll loop in @Alex from sales after the sync.
Liam Chen: putting follow-up on calendar: 16:00 UTC tomorrow 30m. invite sent to participants.
SRE Pager: IncidentBot: incident resolved and transitioned to post-incident. Remember to tag the postmortem with severity and customer impact.
Maya Patel: thanks team. I'll capture the action items in linear/ticketing and assign owners. Please add any more items here.
Ken O'Connor: one more: update runbook snippet with exact kubectl commands we used to inspect pods and queues. paste for runbook: ```
# check model-serving queue length
kubectl get pods -l app=model-serving -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, queueLen: .metadata.annotations.queueLen}'
# check autoscaler events
kubectl -n infra describe hpa model-serving
```
Priya Singh: added note about fallback verification: make sure 100% traffic to fallback in a canary before rolling rules back.
Maya Patel: that's it for now. closing the incident thread and moving to postmortem doc. :white_check_mark: 
Ken O'Connor: closing notes: runbook PR id will be linked in the postmortem. thanks all. :heart:
